title: No Hotline, No Refunds: Self-Custody Loss Is Final
plain:
Self-custody means you hold the keys and carry all of the responsibility yourself. There is no company behind your wallet, no customer service department, and no manager who can step in when something goes wrong.

The hard truth is that there is no hotline that can recover lost self-custodied bitcoin. If your keys or backups are destroyed, stolen, or simply forgotten, those funds are effectively gone. Bitcoin has no password reset, no fraud department, and no chargebacks.

Scammers exploit exactly this. Anyone advertising a 'recovery service' that promises to bring back lost bitcoin is lying — they want your money or your seed words. Never share, type, or photograph your seed words for anyone offering help.

Because of this finality, deciding how much bitcoin to hold in self-custody is a serious money decision, like any large purchase or investment. For money decisions like this, talk to a licensed financial advisor who can look at your whole situation before you commit a large amount.

A licensed advisor cannot recover lost bitcoin either, and a genuine one will never ask for your keys or seed words. What they can do is help you think about how much to hold, how it fits your goals, and how much risk you can honestly carry.

Until you are confident, go slowly: practice with small amounts, keep written backups somewhere safe and private, and verify every address before sending. In self-custody, careful habits are your only safety net.
technical:
Bitcoin removes trusted third parties, which also removes recovery paths. Transactions are finalized by network consensus with no administrative override, and keys are derived from a BIP39/BIP32 seed, so losing the seed (and any passphrase) leaves funds on-chain but permanently unspendable. No miner, developer, or company can reassign them; backup redundancy and inheritance planning are the only real mitigations.

'Crypto recovery' scams target people who have lost access, charging upfront fees or requesting seed words to 'diagnose' a wallet. Legitimate professionals, including licensed financial advisors, work on planning and allocation, never key recovery, and never need your seed words. Treat a large move into self-custody as you would any major financial decision and seek licensed advice first.
